A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Visual Planning/VPRL work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–D are readable and support a reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original planning experiments on FrozenLake, Maze, and MiniBehavior, including benchmark scores, training analyses, ablations, and out-of-distribution results.

after.justification: v2 retains original planning results and adds textual-baseline experiments, layout-error measurements, and qualitative masked-input evaluations.

M1.justification: The proposed procedure retains random-trajectory initialization, autoregressive image prediction, GRPO, and the same progress/validity rewards. Renaming the parser and progress map as a dynamics interpreter and progress estimator does not change their implementation. Alternative neural interpreters are discussed as possible extensions.

E1.justification: The three navigation tasks and existing larger-grid evaluations remain. v2 adds a limited qualitative scenario involving partially occluded inputs, using black/gray masks across the retained environments (Appendix C.4, Figure 12).

E2.justification: v2 substantially broadens the FrozenLake comparisons with coordinate-based and ASCII-based textual SFT variants, plus textual GRPO using either VPRL-style progress rewards or PR rewards. These are evaluated for both Qwen 3B and 7B in Table 7, beyond v1's direct SFT and inference-only textual baselines.

E3.justification: The main experiments report LVM/Qwen sizes of 7B instead of 3B. Textual SFT batch size changes from 16 to 4 and gradient accumulation from 2 to 1. EM/PR now explicitly accept any shortest optimal trajectory. New textual RL experiments also introduce evaluation/training protocols. These reported revisions do not establish that retained results were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds substantial diagnostic evidence: textual representation and reward-design ablations, quantitative layout-mismatch analysis, textual reasoning case studies, and masked-input robustness examples (Section 4; Appendices C.2 and C.4). The existing initialization, exploration, VPFT*, and larger-grid analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions show Gaussian-smoothed reward curves with standard deviations across response groups (Figure 7, Appendix C.1). v2 adds no independent-run or seed reporting, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces Qwen-3B SFT averages of 34.3% EM/53.3% PR with Qwen-7B results of 53.6%/69.9%; these are different reported settings. VPRL's 80.6%/84.9% averages remain numerically unchanged. v2 adds extensive textual-ablation scores and coordinate/ASCII layout-mismatch rates of 25.7%/22.3%, substantially revising the comparative evidence.

T1.justification: Section 3 revises the mathematical definitions of EM and PR from matching a single reference trajectory to maximizing over the set of shortest optimal trajectories. This is a limited formal-definition change; the training objectives remain equivalent, and no proofs or theorems are added.

C1.justification: The headline efficacy claim is materially narrowed: v1 presents visual SFT as substantially superior, whereas v2 distinguishes comparable visual/textual SFT from VPRL's advantage. The introduction/conclusion reduce the headline advantage from over 40 to 27 percentage points, and the abstract reframes visual planning as a supplement for vision-first tasks.

C2.justification: v2 extends the existing modality-gap interpretation with textual layout errors and explains how summed progress rewards poorly distinguish action order. It also interprets masked-input traces and discusses neural validators as future extensions. The principal exploration explanation and existing limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendices B.4, C.2, and D add textual-RL hyperparameters, format rewards, sequence padding/normalization rules, and coordinate/ASCII/GRPO prompts. Existing parser, hardware, and code-access disclosures remain. However, v2 omits the exact Gemini model-version identifiers supplied in v1 Section 3.

R1.justification: v2 adds four world/dynamics-model references and an action-conditional generative-model discussion, distinguishing its holistic planner from predictors requiring external planning. The existing visual-reasoning and RL positioning, including the principal novelty claims, is largely retained.

P1.justification: The overall narrative and section sequence remain recognizable. Selected abstract, reward, results, and limitations passages are rewritten; terminology is revised; v1 Section 2.3 moves to Appendix B.4; and a dedicated textual-baseline subsection is inserted into Appendix C.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 2 and 7, textual-output Figures 8–9, and masked-input Figure 12. It adds an RL column to the hyperparameter table and relocates retained displays. These extend the existing presentation without broadly redesigning its figures or visual style.

improvement.justification: The stronger textual comparator and new representation/reward controls in Tables 1, 2, and 7 improve the empirical argument, while acknowledging SFT parity makes the conclusions better calibrated. Explicit treatment of multiple optimal paths also improves evaluation clarity. These gains are limited by unreconciled model-size/metric revisions accompanying unchanged visual scores and the loss of exact Gemini version identifiers.
